verdict.rationale: Superset ships first-party ways to drive the product in natural language. The prompt-first flow turns a described task into a running agent workspace. The `superset:orchestrate` skill lets an agent take a plain-language instruction ("split this migration into independent slices and run a worker on each") and operate Superset through its CLI. The official MCP server lets agents create workspaces, launch sessions, schedule automations and manage tasks. However, natural-language control runs through a third-party coding agent rather than a native command interface, and one user describes the product as terminal-centric rather than chat-centric. Missing for 10: a native natural-language command interface for operating the app itself, documentation of which app operations are reachable via natural language, and independent hands-on corroboration of natural-language-driven orchestration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: In the prompt-first flow, describe the task, pick an agent, and create. The agent starts working on your prompt immediately.
The `superset:orchestrate` skill lets one agent coordinate workers in separate workspaces through the Superset CLI.
Fan out a refactor or migration across several worktrees at once ("split this migration into independent slices and run a worker on each")
Superset MCP server: create Git-worktree workspaces, launch coding-agent sessions, schedule automations, open terminals, and manage tasks on behalf of a Superset user.
Use **Design** in the browser pane to select an element and send your requested change to an agent with element context.
